# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4976%2E898137%2EBhMj-3)
Are you tired of Democrats playing defense, ? I know I am.
[](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/952?c0=mam-em-june2026.kcuFj4&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260613_PM2_V1_S1&t=2&akid=4976%2E898137%2EBhMj-3)
Democratic messaging usually sounds something like this: “Democrats are fighting to help you put food on the table.”
Now look, of course that’s true, but that vision isn’t big enough. Being against Donald Trump is simply not enough.
We need to think bigger, dream bigger, and lay out a vision for the New American Dream that people can see themselves in, something they want to vote for. A Michigan where you know you’ll have a tight knit community, where you don’t have to just get by, but afford the life you dreamed of.
While Donald Trump wants to burn it all to the ground, we have to build something new — something that works for everyone.
That’s why I first ran for office, even when everyone told me I couldn’t win. It’s why I flipped a seat that my opponent had won by 16 points in the previous election. Just about everyone told me I’d lose. But we did the actual work, organized, and won a seat that nobody thought we could touch.
I know how to beat MAGA extremists because I’ve actually gone toe-to-toe with them and won. Now, I’m bringing that same strategy to my run for the U.S. Senate.
This month is incredibly important for this campaign. Ballots drop in exactly **12 DAYS** , and we are staring down our final end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before the primary.

Jun 14

If you have seen my campaign before, you'll know we have jumped through countless hoops, the latest being gerrymandered into a different district. **We have kept the same fight up, but sometimes I get asked: " Mike, why are you doing this?"**
For me the answer has never changed. It's the families I've sat across from in diners across three counties who are working harder than any generation before them and still can't get ahead. It's the young people inheriting a country that feels more broken than promised. It's every person who has ever sat in a doctor's office, or a kitchen table, or a car in a parking lot trying to figure out how to make the numbers work and wondered whether anyone in Washington even knows they exist.
**I know they exist. Because I 've been one of them.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/b64ffa2d-8470-4198-9cee-8032fda73d83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Our fight is based on the real struggles our communities face, and I won 't tap out until I get **_**you**_**a seat at the table on Capitol Hill.[Can I rely on a $20 donation today to make that happen this year?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96f9b539-6f88-4961-8006-ac13734ce45c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Help Us Out HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96f9b539-6f88-4961-8006-ac13734ce45c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This campaign was never about defeating one politician. It was about proving that a different kind of politics is possible. One built on honesty, on showing up, on fighting for people who have been waiting too long for someone to fight for them.
We have built something real here. Something that belongs to every person who has chipped in, shared a post, knocked a door, or simply believed that this district could be better represented.
**Don 't stop now.**

Today is Flag Day. We honor the American flag—not as a decoration, not as a political emblem, but as a sacred reminder of what generations before us sacrificed to preserve. The flag represents a nation built on the promise that government exists by the consent of the governed. It represents liberty under law, rights given by God, and the responsibility of every citizen to protect the republic entrusted to us. At Unite4Freedom, we believe honoring the flag means more than flying it. It means defending the principles it stands for: Real voters. Real votes. Real counts. Real proof. A free nation cannot survive without trustworthy elections, lawful process, transparent records, and citizens willing to stand in the gap. This Flag Day, may we remember that freedom is not self-sustaining. It must be guarded, verified, and passed on with courage. We do not stand for a party. We stand for the republic. We stand for the Constitution. We stand for every lawful American vote. May God bless America, and may we be found faithful in preserving what the flag represents.

body:
Here's what's happening at Defenders of Wildlife

Here's what's happening at Defenders of Wildlife
                  

                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5627335/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5627336/38SyG9Xl)

WILDLIFE IN THE NEWS

“This administration is brutally sacrificing eons-old habitat for mother polar bears and cubs, calving grounds for caribou and nesting habitat for millions of migratory birds, all in the name of oil and gas gains that may never be realized.”

Nicole Whittington-Evans, senior Alaska and Northwest program director, on last week’s oil lease sale in the Arctic Refuge.

Read Here → (https://support.defenders.org/s/5627337/38SyG9Xl)

 

Protect Arctic Wildlife: Tell BLM Not to Weaken Wildlife Protections in the NPR-A!

The Bureau of Land Management is now deciding whether to fast-track oil and gas development in a massive stretch of wildlife habitat known as the National Petroleum Alaska-Reserve, which is home to an incredible array of animals, including caribou, polar bears, migratory birds and more. These animals are currently protected by safeguards that BLM could decide to weaken, putting their lives and homes in danger. Keep polar bears and other Arctic animals safe: Tell BLM not to weaken vital protections for wildlife in the Reserve! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5627338/38SyG9Xl)

 

Stay Smart: Do’s and Don’ts of Exploring in Wolf Country (https://support.defenders.org/s/5627339/38SyG9Xl)

The prospect of seeing a wolf has inspired countless tourists to lace up their boots and make the trip to wild places like Yellowstone. From identifying tracks to learning what to do if you spot a wolf, we share tips on how recreate safely and responsibly in wolf country!

Read More → (https://support.defenders.org/s/5627340/38SyG9Xl)

From the Blue Ridge Mountains to the depths of its caves, Tennessee is a state that is home to some incredible animals, particularly salamanders. Learn what natural features make Tennessee so hospitable to these iconic amphibians and how humans can keep them from harm.

Shorebirds of Delaware Bay (https://support.defenders.org/s/5627345/38SyG9Xl)

The Delaware Bay is a super-highway for flocks of shorebirds! Sandpipers, red knots and countless others migrate through in the spring on the way to their breeding grounds in the Arctic. Find out what makes this waterway a birdwatcher’s paradise, and why protecting horseshoe crabs is so important to this ecosystem.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | Today's Top Pick (ads) | • | Salem Media Group ---|--- • | Safe Money Report • | Weiss Ratings | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ## Judge Blocks Paxton's ActBlue Suit
A federal judge [Thursday blocked](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO6yAURVeDO1tACDgFxW_c5bdTWs_wSNBgY8FzcHY_ymxh-qt7dM7Xfb5DTHF7_IcVLZ0hzxu2mpAIy1z3o1SXU4K9YgLC6gq2lsssudQ9171Qs4eY3rPqvF24v4kOrTCjUBd102P3tPxmuBg5-LCYBQxo7rRxKAS_Ggzoumg_Z1wLJQSXSg9LUFcDSgH3owGUTHH0kXIZ6ImEJ9SQ3vmFZXB57ZJ9Eu2VXf4xOTE5tdaGkE8DR6W4fSZMTh8nJqcdTspbv6TsvtH3oeS1r0fcHj04WtKBXbF-bzGlWLVhij9WiOkXQ3-L87LyJwAA__-9wnu3) Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, R, from pursuing his lawsuit against Democrat fundraising platform ActBlue, granting a preliminary injunction on [free speech grounds](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO6yAURVeDOywgBJyC4jfu8tsprRfziJlgY8FzSHY_ymxh6itdnXO-rtMVYorb_T-s6OgV8rRhqwmJsEx1P0qdc0qwV0xAWOeCreUyKaEMF4ZLPXmI6T3pzrub8BfZoZN2kPqkL2boFjcPJnjvlThLALAG_SVYawaBwZ6EnrvoPmfCSC2lUNr0t6DPFrQG4QcLqJgW6CPl0tOChC-oIb3zE0s_57VLbiHaKzv9Y2pkamyt9Q-q62dkavzYMDV-H_6OvBwJK3_gxnd4Ud74DNuWia_5iTzk0qB43iItHGa6pQN5glaPSEyNXXF-bzGlWI1lWtxXiOmXgP7W7enUTwAAAP__d_OFrg). District Judge Richard Stearns ruled the suit [was retaliation](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3SAQBdCvwR0WzGPxc0GRxt2mTWmNYWyTYLAAL96_j_ZF-YLtphgd3Xt_vc_v6IOP2088yNR7TXOkVgLVSnku55WLTSHgWShgpWIztZbyDAI0F5pLNTv04XNWnTOLcKPsyMjhKdVDjfrZ7eax0NuoNFpcR-HcONgB1lGDkiMggu28-cKElkpKAUr3y6reBlQKhXsOSMCUIOdryn3dqdKNZQ2f6YNyb9PRBbPXehb2-MFgYjC11vqGZfdxqynSjYeP_14ZTF_dGEwWjxP9Fl93ilumUnyKGBhMSgsNEhhMvy-3EV9Csn8KP_GuKfJy-bhxtHUJF_GKAbO3if8HuU3RUn7BXTbubD4EX_TAlNgO9OEVuX5v6A8DfwMAAP__I4mWlA) for ActBlue's fundraising for state Rep. James Talarico, D-Austin, who is challenging Paxton for a U.S. Senate seat. Stearns noted Paxton's 2023 investigation sat dormant until Talarico raised over $2.5 million in 24 hours after a TV appearance, about $2.2 million through ActBlue. The ruling bars Paxton from refiling. His office alleged the platform allowed foreign and fraudulent donations.
## Texas GOP Ousts Chair
Texas Republicans [ousted party Chairman Abraham George](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOiPbTIxTuNiG7m67JRrwAJYGjGwnTt5-lbzC7b8fnfPvZ_rBwOHc_uJBrrzWOJ1UM1MplKZ8PVJeIjNemRgL5SVRrTFNWmojpBEKJo-B3xO03s3S31VLTg1WQQ93Y9vd3aw3YBfo77MdVomz7dGCGYwapJ1vaxvcZ0waBUpJDaabV7gNCIDS2wFJNyDJhxJTV3Yq9MK88js-KXVLPFp2eylXbvo_jR4bPdZauzW-tNnjI5d4fkKNHj9UjR6_dZHoeswcFjzFham8hU_h9CgSnh6ZBc4JdzzERjFt1CbnrxqYQzZDA3I7MPD3u_zO2NPp_wEAAP__gYaC1g) at their state convention in Houston on Friday, replacing him with his former running mate, D'Rinda Randall, giving the party its fifth chair in six years. Randall, who served as vice chair under George, defeated him after delegates expressed frustration that he was too close to the party's establishment wing. David Covey will serve as her vice chair. The convention also advanced a harder-line platform, with delegates backing priorities including closing the state's primary system and restricting the spread of Islamic law. Governor Greg Abbott used his keynote to [outline a fourth-term agenda](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykULuu2zAM_Rp5YyApih-Dhy7ebteOBi3RsXAVyxBZ6-bvC-cXuhAEDs7zz9f8hTHF_fkbXzTKz5rnnSonEqEy8_G3sM8p4cGUUIh9oVpzma22LegWjJsDxvSeXRPGRYfBNDSarjfu7oa2b7bRkF6t633oh653Hd77dXjcqV36wS7BPZo4XmK6Nc4YbV17W1b36NA51KHvkKxymkKUXG6ykdAP8pre-aRy8_nVpHETOVjdfyk7KTvVWm_fjHKByk5XG2WnD03Z6bJSdtLXMVbZCQWe-QCf95N2iXkHXJYsAmeuDJIh0CunyNvn8QWFwWNKDGsu4Av675DrDnmHDcwCZ2RkwD0Ab1giQsKq7NSUMRw1phS57ZTTzxfG9Mkv_7f6Odp_AQAA__8nwZhF), vowing to "demolish the Democrats" and push restrictions on H-1B visas. The multiday event at Houston's George R. Brown Convention Center drew thousands of delegates and concluded on Saturday.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

# Just The Truth
Your No-BS Newsletter Dear Readers, Today's sponsor, PreBorn!, is working to connect women facing unexpected pregnancies with free ultrasounds, compassionate support, and life-affirming resources at a moment when many feel they have nowhere else to turn. Thank you for your consideration of our sponsors.
The Just The Truth Team
* * *
[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/%2BIL77Qm%2BdIpOoiflKP1w5QE2JvKYjQ5O0XZgK2YffBhCWzdXXj3I35utYZzv%0ASANA76ruWKazbHKn4%2BHbrCyzgw8ftCr0KfAIvphNQDL4wUUQLNf45jpyxndZ%0AryATxUEA4%2FCPUHUqyGImctl1R6i37yyGTd0x2D2584Al1%2Bx59Cp4bfUgOcgY%0AKQcjDfuU1WB0nh0Rsyggmr0eNBajEix2Gg%3D%3D%0A/84b74e321eadd15c)Advocate for Life,The abortion pill was already sitting in her online cart when she found PreBorn!.She had spent most of the night scrolling through websites that promised an easy solution to her fear. Everything she read made the process sound clinical, detached, and uncomplicated—as though ending a pregnancy was no more significant than filling a prescription.But underneath the panic and late-night searching was a woman who felt completely trapped.She wasn’t thinking about politics. She was thinking about rent. About disappointing her parents. About whether the father would disappear if she kept the baby. About how alone she felt carrying a secret she didn’t know how to tell anyone.And like so many women today, she was being pushed toward abortion before anyone had even shown her her baby.[**That is why PreBorn!’s ministry is so urgent right now.**](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/2oiTaaVZaaErrIKxJFpTgROrTbOPefm27oC%2BNSXEBUSbn3mRTgo5BjmTOkbz%0AkOaM5bzaMtejmkuOIfUDGr6WP9gcp9eBx7ypfFwgqGXPkaeC%2BODiQbrtzLMJ%0AKKxK06ToTuHPhBszuyJP%2F4bg7%2FUQd1K%2BmBhHjsvD%2F1jAwSGAv6ZXBGq6If2S%0AY4kqd3pSrNghOAx0xihvXeRx3%2F4T67Oeog%3D%3D%0A/d1547d9cb52655a3) More abortions than ever are happening through pills ordered quickly and privately, often without an ultrasound and without meaningful counseling. The entire system is built around speed. Move fast. Don’t think too long. Solve the problem before the emotions catch up.At PreBorn!, we step into the middle of that rush and offer something radically different.We offer her a chance to pause.A chance to ask questions.
A chance to be heard.

# Sunday, June 14, 2026

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1775, the Continental Congress authorized the formation of the Continental Army, enlisting skilled riflemen to serve the United Colonies for one year. This decision established what [would become the U.S. Army](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO2yAURp8Gb1hwISQeGLp4S9eO1g1cDC02EdBYfvvKXf4H-PdPR-c7v57LE1NO-_oTN7I9lGWno2Xqneqy4r5mQk_1T8qZPL5LbS5SW0CA4cJwqRePKZ-LHrwNREBqICvvD6m1kFoO0T6EcVoIUlpP4WUESlBGopD3KTglxJDsRRNGagkwCTnKcBPOT-oBwaOBO9OCfOqljr9L2nukkM_yoTq6sg3Zxt7fjakfDGYG83Ec4_5yB7aY9rWX_VoxmK9bDOZcHGYG89_GsW4nj6n1Uk8e0PXG4SZ65K9Ue_R48i8I947BrCYFctIM5qFa_z5SzqmZy2_dMOX_Pv1bET8W_gUAAP__nE-FTg), more than a year before the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776. You might recall _Highlights_ magazine from a childhood trip to the dentist's or doctor's office. The publication began modestly in the 1940s and grew into a thriving publication with millions of readers over the decades. But you might be surprised to read the rest of the story in today’s [Whatever Happened To...](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGnMd0iezAsW7i4VxEpkk0bKQ0a7DE4GfDKthaRp482r5D-6DvS_34drxg4bPMbrmSKj-NGe2YqhdI44zYzoaP0FZjJ4S2mbBfKI0joTrI7KT06DHyMunLGEwE1FRl17pXWUmlVLaaVdprUhGDP02SpUU3ftxakbNHa1vdVMA9NdkorgItUtfKttO7S9OAddnAWWpILJab6M4atLOT5iHdKtY1rxWYp5ZZF80_AIGDY970OWy44J1wfCwFDImIBw9PHa_t8fOf_x4uAoUrG3fbAHHL3uJhXDPxLlj91uBv4CQAA__9MTXEm) section. In case you missed it, this week on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla Brown broke down the clearest guidance yet on alcohol consumption and health. Scientists have debated for years whether a daily drink helps or harms you, and a major new study offered fresh answers. Ayla explained what the latest research found and what it could mean for your long-term health. [Listen here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MFugzAQBNCvMbcg79qYcPAhUpRbWvXSHtGC1-DWwSk40Px9RX-h1xnpjTQf1_ZKIYZpeKEb2-xTO_G2RM6Z53agaYhMjuevECM7uqd56UdeWpRoDtIcQLeOQny2unDWMyOrgi3UR9BagoZitIbr2gATSNkgNV5L8l2PnaeOZWWqIthdkwY0IDYSSvCV7F2jjugdGayFluxCTnP5mcKUR_bxmVaeyz7dimjHnO-LUCeBF4GXbdvKZ3rkR8d7vyeU-1GoyyrUWX8_fk7rO7y-nQSaLNRZVXIpZuvuW4gxLGZfG24U4p-e_3XJavE3AAD__58wc7U). We’re the most informed humans who have ever existed... but we’re also the most anxious. Our human hardware was never designed to take in all that the 24/7 news cycle throws at us. That’s why we read [_The Pour Over_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1qwzAUBeCnsbcEXUmx40FDIWRL147iRrqylerHyHJC3r44tOQBuh344HA4Xxd9QR98Gj8xkqou60SPJVCtVPSIaQyElsq3D4EszrksZqJFc8a7Het2ILVFH55atlY5Ik6iJQX9EaRkIKGdlEFyg4CrEwZhwMGxno4dEz2DKxxgaL3a2lgHEjgfGOzBHZixgzhyZ7HjfSMZWV9z2d-yT3UiF575TmVvcmyDmmqdl0Z8NPzc8POf1YnmvJZXzmXcUJzXGvWS12KoEad3UcO7TSJZv8ZGnN4X_IrBOKMf02ZYfU4Y9G1NpEG2Rdn54UPwS7ctHSP68FpW_3XnXfGfAAAA__8qXoxb).

## US Strike Kills Tren de Aragua Leader
President Trump announced late Friday that a U.S. strike has killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, [the leader of Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu6zAQRL9G6mjwZVIqWNzGnW-bUlhzlxKT1QMULcP5-kD5hZSDAQbnzMd9uEPmvIz_YaZQ0zos9NqZaqUyjLCMTIBUvjIzIWxr2eNE-6CldkI6oeyAkPk92BZDItJkWgrKd8paqaxqp5BUtIbAdM6TsSgxGWdcgk7HR98Btjmca9Ipq7TupbqodJURe9PphOC0b6wkzHUtl881L3WixO_1oHKJ69xymGrd9sb8a_St0TfYToGzOkOpOTI1-lbLc95ELbQIJAEFxieI008ctND3kxiEsRYfzmGC2HlMPkJv8OoJvI941bItAbdXZs67O6HGGTL_QtQ_PXcE_RMAAP__5cGCGQ). In a social media post, Trump called the action a "swift and lethal kinetic strike." The post included [a video showing a building explode](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MFq8zAQBOCnsW4Jq7UiOwcdfvjxLT0VejRba2WrXVtGUhLy9sV9hV5n4BuYj9t4oyhxm99oZVdDGjd-FuFaOY8zbbMwec7fUYQ97SmXaeEyIqA9gT1pM3qK8hqN8i4wI7eKne56bQxoo9XiEKlDBG0xfHZm6j0yTxQ89-ShQ1DRHRpYbTTiFfRZhwtM_tr2GDxZ7BoD7GNN-fyV4lYXDvJKD87nKa1K3FLrXpr2X4NDg0PN97qUNEWSoz9CA5lJ_qeNxL_n-7o3OOyp1NLgoLXtDGi4QN-2pgcwKju_P6NILPaYnleKv5Sqf_rn4fAnAAD__0jTd0Q) and become engulfed in flames and smoke. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said the strike was made earlier in the week, ["in full collaboration with Venezuelan security forces."](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFy8yAQhJ8GdXjgjLFcUPyNOv9tSs1FHOISBB7A9jhPn1HyCKl3Zne_7-06X5ET5_U_buR6KHOmZ0vUO9V5xbwmQk_1k1Mij7dS2xKpzaDASmWlNrNHTq_ZDN4FIqDjQE6fR22M0kYP0akRg9LjQufx5K2l5R3JKrAYAqKCMLDb25TVRgNclD7ocFKLvxxHCB4tnIVR5LmXevgonHukkF7lQfWwlG1ILvZ-a-L4T8AkYOqRIqe0ZwKmWDbagQRM6DfO3HrFziULmE4XAGtGeW9y48Qd60vunE0-KNPXnRJmuSuQvw4ETEN1_vbklLjZ_da6If9MDf1P7h4OvgMAAP__04SEog) Guerrero Flores was confirmed dead in the strike. Since September, the administration has targeted alleged Tren de Aragua gang members, [striking dozens of alleged drug smuggling boats](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAQhp8Gb0RwJsYZGLp4S9eOFvUdNg0GC3Aiv33l5hG63HLSp-_7v-7j3frg4_xpVzLVpTHSqwSqlfI42zgHskj54UMgtFvKZVqojCCg46LjUo1ofThG1aBxREBtQ0bqXiolpJLNYjRdUWuNDr8BJytUr8kpdG2PWoK6Nd6cNNFJJQFuQl6ku4oJb20PDm0HmilB6GvKl5_kY13IhSM9KV-mtDbBLLVuhbUfDAYGQzy2VOr5YjCcYAaDOI8EBsNe-NnHYKiZIkfiNtt5t_ydyaOPic875Uw58Xc195HvhVufS83-Qbzmfd14scfJabLB7eVD8KU7TefV-vBnVv8159PAbwAAAP__WdOJog) and killing more than 200 suspected narcoterrorists.
## Switzerland to Vote on Population Cap
After decades of embracing free movement and foreign investment, Switzerland will vote on Sunday on [whether to cap its population at 10 million.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkb2u3CAQRp8Gd1iAMXdduNgocnfTJFJKa2LGhiwGC2YXbZ4-Iq-QajQ_OtKZ7-fn-gk--Hh8gxNn2tMasZaARJjXA-IRECzmhw8BLVwpl81hWZVQhgvDpV4t-PBedWfnHVHh0OEsP25SayG17NxsDUhhNjvtoKwexmk0I2gz3CY5KfsLOz83mjBSS6UmIXu5j2Kz03BTuwWjPpgWaD2l3P9OPpLDPbzTC3O_pbMLsyO6ChvuTC1MLbXW_iyx7ZhaMPJnYWo5U8R3q5AfSG1Sqqc_mANEy33hr0Q-HjxFXh2Sw8wp8Q0u7qnwK13PAORT5EBcCn76EFrnMGPh1QG180dMlakFMr_f1Vh_-JMNS9q8ZcPXL-3FWMt3zFeXZ3vVhiimyR0n-PBPhv4rgdes_gYAAP__nvic2w) The country's population has grown far faster than any surrounding European Union states, [rising by 23% since the free movement agreement](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpiAQhJ8Gb_yBlsHxwGEv3mavezQttMpsCwZwzLz9xn2FuVUqlaov9edj_sDIMW2_8SDX1jwnuitTa1TmDdPGhIHK38hMAc9cqt-pzqDASmWlNnPAyN-z6YJbiYD6jpwe3rUxShvd7c6D92YwSvm3xSoPdllGG3AIerVqhL6L7mlTVhsNMCr90uub8mHs32ENaGEQRlGILZfXZ46p7bTyd_6i8vL56NjtrZ1V9L8ETAKm-75fbaftwhIipifzuLlwEDA9SwKmzysJmHQvYKp3rFXeGJtsWe6ERRaqFzeZV7kgc24yJ-nxPGPa5JnPi7HFnCQ2qZU8InPMqSsunPejq32AtwMj_wdsP3r1y8G_AAAA__9OQ4x9) came into effect in 2002. Close to 27% of Swiss residents are not citizens. Supporters of the population restrictions say the influx of mainly EU workers puts housing, schools, transportation, welfare, and the Swiss way of life under unbearable strain. Critics argue that Switzerland [benefits from closer EU ties](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFu8zAMBeDTyJsDkVbkeNDwL97yrx0F1iJttYoVyEqC3L5Qr9CFAx_wPeB9XP2VYor7-p9u7Kpkv_PrSFwrF7_SviamwOU7psSB7rkcy8aHR42217YH4wPF9PamC06YkYeOHYwXMEaDgW5zIDQuMJkwnpmEBGT4RDPKOYiQ5amLrmnaggHEScMJ5KyXMA0XlEAWR2U0h1hzOX3luNeNJb3zk8tpybcuua3W-6GGfwpnhbPkUh87t0zh3GSFs24HtMKZHjX3oZDUvv264sL9FVOKh209641i-nXrn8Z4OvwJAAD__9zIcP8) and gets needed labor, expertise, and skills from foreigners in sectors like healthcare, finance, pharmaceuticals, and technology.
## Knicks Snap Title Drought
The New York Knicks battled back from another double-digit deficit to [win the franchise's first NBA championship](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Ltu7CAQxvGnwd1azBhfKChOg3SKTZsSzZrBJsEXAVpr3z7avELqT_p90v_z7u4UU9yXD9rY1HC4na-SuFbObqF9SUye83dMiT2dRy7zysWhxOEmhxso5ymml1ONN4EZuWvYwDiBUhIUNKuR4aFpHGHSnXz4aewnRJh18HLGHrVuonlrcgAFiFpCC6GXs9fdhMHTgKNQkn2sR26_jrjXlUN6HU_O7XxsTTJrrWcR3T-BVqC9rqvlcu7vUaDdHyTQZp7pFGidQLvQxv-9QKskTL3Ww9hk488rphTL8D5bNorpF69_KvI0-BMAAP__A21xoQ) in 53 years, beating the San Antonio Spurs 94-90 on the road. One game removed from the [biggest comeback in NBA Finals history](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOgzAQRU9jOpA9OIYULrahy7ZbogGPYTbGRtgKyu1X5Apbf72vp_fzGB_IgePyjRvZ4tMY6cyBSqFjXDAugdDR8eQQyOGejjyvlEeQYGppaqVHhxzeo66c9URAbUVWdb3SWiqtqtWaDkyrSCvqZq8QPHXUk_d4l11_66lie71Jo7QCuEvVKH-Ts7u3PXiHBjqhJTku6Wh-E8eykg_v9KKjmdNWBbuWsmfRfgkYBAzneTaU93iNAoY4oYAhl3S8BQyjgIGdgEHLtu2MNBewYqknXhbKpZ7TRhPOz1zHCWvPEUOuV_7w1WHdfnIInM3ltGzI4eNQ_hXuZeEvAAD__6QigV8) in Game 4, New York again trailed by double digits in the second half. A 15-2 run with less than four minutes remaining in the fourth gave the Knicks their first lead since the first quarter. After the Spurs fought back to tie, [Jalen Brunson's floater](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u8yAUxvGrwVsizuHDMDC8rypvydrRIuZg0xLbApo0d1-5t9D1P_we6Xm_jBefclrnq7-Ta3EbV3rWTK1RGWe_zpl8oPKZcqbg963UaaE6Ikd94voEcgw-5dcou-AiEZLoyEFvQEoOErrFhZuSsheTtBKENzHADeKNpMXJBATVJXdoXIMERMvhDFHxKVhhMAavsWeSU0htK-ePLa1toZhf24PKedruXXZLa3tl4h_DgeHwfVSGw_X_EWrz7asyHJBrZW2v0BitQAmwhomhMvGGvCsu7M-Uc6r6GJvvPuVfvP3pkYfDnwAAAP__W_BvyQ) with a minute remaining put New York ahead. He led all scorers with 45 points and was named the [NBA Finals MVP](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUxvGnwVuiwwEDGRjuVeUtWTsiYg42LTER0KR5-8p9ha7_4fdJ3_vZnX3KaVsu_ka2x-I2erZMvVN1i9-WTD5Q_Uw5U_D3Utu8UnMIqA6gDly64FN-OTkEG4mQxECWa8OlBC75sFph9IkjYDDhqgNclSE9zyoSCq3jyIdkdw0UlxzxBPzI4whzOAmDMXiFmkmgkHqpx4-Str5SzK_yoHqcy23Idu393pj4x3BiOH3vleF0-b-H1n3_agwnBKUApBKj0WY0oOTIxNSYeEMYqg33Z8o5NbWPLTef8i_e__TIw-JPAAAA__8zCm-Z). It's New York's [third NBA championship](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFutDAQBOCngQ7kNf7NUbj4G7pLmxKt8YI3MTayrUP39hF5hdQjfaOZz-fyRA4c9w88yNQtLZGuEqhWysuOcQ-EjvI3h0AOz5TL6qksUkjdCd2BWhxyeC-qdWYjkjS0ZGB8gFICFLTeEMA2gbJuID1aCxOAXfVqJ2FHoZBaNrcmNCiQchLQw_ZPrG4aHnJzqOXYKEGOa8r9V-JYPW3hnV6U-zUdbTC-1rM0w_9Gzo2cr-vqo8U7a-R8j2nk7LnUlN9dtNitHo-TUyxtNu68OAQu-u7YD-Twa9Y_HfEy8icAAP__9mtycA), following titles in 1970 and 1973.

**Whatever happened to _Highlights_ magazine?** Picture every doctor's office of your childhood. The vinyl chairs. The fish tank, maybe. And on the table, [a copy of _Highlights for Children_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGnMd0iezAsW7i4VxEpkk0bKQ0a7DE4GfDKthaRp482r5D-6DvS_34drxg4bPMbrmSKj-NGe2YqhdI44zYzoaP0FZjJ4S2mbBfKI0joTrI7KT06DHyMunLGEwE1FRl17pXWUmlVLaaVdprUhGDP02SpUU3ftxakbNHa1vdVMA9NdkorgItUtfKttO7S9OAddnAWWpILJab6M4atLOT5iHdKtY1rxWYp5ZZF80_AIGDY970OWy44J1wfCwFDImIBw9PHa_t8fOf_x4uAoUrG3fbAHHL3uJhXDPxLlj91uBv4CQAA__9MTXEm). For millions of American kids, _Highlights_ was the first magazine they ever read, usually while waiting for a shot or the dentist's drill. For children, it was an escape. They hunted for the hidden pictures (a toothbrush tucked into a tree branch, a slice of pie hiding in a cloud). And everyone checked in on [Goofus and Gallant](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd7Hg8cCmoNjGXbbd0iLmYbMhxgImVv5-5PmFqe_VvUfn332-u5jivv51L7It5HmnsyZqjcq8un1N5DyVZ0yJvDtyqctGdQYO-sb1TeDsXUyfGTtvAxGQ7MiKYRSIXKDoNkuBeylHJQMq76TkAz6EDxAeSo1aQxfttca1QAFguOhFUHzxRo4QvNMwMOTkY8ul_5_j3jYK6ZPfVPolv7pkt9aOyuQfBhOD6TzPPriFHjk_rwKDaS3566gMJinAABpQSiuDyGA6cm1XAsoMykipOUpAIRhMXbH-OGNKseoLYX25mH4u2688vS18BwAA__9R3nbi), the two boys who faced the same situation on every page: the wild Goofus grabbing the last cookie, the polite Gallant offering it to a friend. Husband-and-wife educators Garry Cleveland Myers and Caroline Clark Myers launched the magazine in June 1946 from Honesdale, Pennsylvania, and when it nearly folded a few years later, their son quit his job as an aeronautical engineer to rescue it. His big idea? Mail copies to doctors' and dentists' offices. Circulation hit one million in 1971, peaked near three million in the 1980s, and in 2006 the Postal Service delivered the one-billionth copy--all without ever printing a single ad. So whatever happened to it? Here's the surprise: nothing. The magazine turns 80 this month, still owned and run by the founders' family, four generations in, and still edited out of little Honesdale, the same small town where it all began. Highlights now publishes six magazines with a combined circulation of about a million a month, including spinoffs for babies, preschoolers, and puzzle-loving tweens. And the company isn't just hanging on; it's growing. This April, [_Highlights_ and Google](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGy2yAQRb9G6vAIzEN2QZFG3UubUoPZBTZvxXqAPI__PqP8Qvozd849vz73z0BMNf8MB_qRZK_46oxjYNtzqJkxALYvYkYIT2k9Fuy7WYxTi1Pa7hCI37udwSdEg9cZvV5v2tpFWz0X_wFxDetqNWgHNzAxodX2YZJe7wkfbiZ_ri1OW23MfdEXnT6WCPfrzSQIzqyTXRBoSLv8FqqjYOK3fGO7RDlm9mWMZ5-uPyazTWYLj-ikvuVP6wR4IpPZzk-T2Vhi4MlshXJhymV0laSpWIihYVWhgsoimVHh8ZQXNiUV1UHMJFV9EXT1olGUVKaKqoeE4636WafPzcPzdaLdncr5CMT_FMd_df325m8AAAD__6TFkH8) announced that their joint online-safety classroom program had reached one million students. A 2018 documentary about the magazine, _44 Pages,_ is [streaming on Prime Video](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAYBOCnMRvI_jEmDB6aVAyRUnXriP7Ev8GNwch2gtKnr-grdLnlpO-k-7oMF3TeLeMHzqSzDcNCW_KUM8VhxGX0hIbi3XlPBtcQ022iNAAHVXJVCjkYdP41yMJoSwRUF6RFexBSciFFMemGowU4qO5qLdk9O6C2a7qramrT8MLpXeNKSAHQcVEJ2_Cb6eoDWIMKWiY5GZdDrL6DW_JE1r_Ck2J1C3Ph9ZTzmlj9xqBn0G_bVuGMP2HZawa9lOUnjpTK88O8yuMj3olBb1YG_ZG3x_P7CeSpiNqsm_PeJbXvjTM6_-fnf53y1PAbAAD__1G5c-8). But you could still just look around next time you're stuck in a pediatrician's waiting room. Picture every doctor's office of your childhood. The vinyl chairs. The fish tank, maybe. And on the table, . For millions of American kids, Highlights was the first magazine they ever read, usually while waiting for a shot or the dentist's drill. For children, it was an escape. They hunted for the hidden pictures (a toothbrush tucked into a tree branch, a slice of pie hiding in a cloud). And everyone checked in on , the two boys who faced the same situation on every page: the wild Goofus grabbing the last cookie, the polite Gallant offering it to a friend. Husband-and-wife educators Garry Cleveland Myers and Caroline Clark Myers launched the magazine in June 1946 from Honesdale, Pennsylvania, and when it nearly folded a few years later, their son quit his job as an aeronautical engineer to rescue it. His big idea? Mail copies to doctors' and dentists' offices. Circulation hit one million in 1971, peaked near three million in the 1980s, and in 2006 the Postal Service delivered the one-billionth copy--all without ever printing a single ad. So whatever happened to it? Here's the surprise: nothing. The magazine turns 80 this month, still owned and run by the founders' family, four generations in, and still edited out of little Honesdale, the same small town where it all began. Highlights now publishes six magazines with a combined circulation of about a million a month, including spinoffs for babies, preschoolers, and puzzle-loving tweens. And the company isn't just hanging on; it's growing. This April, announced that their joint online-safety classroom program had reached one million students. A 2018 documentary about the magazine, 44 Pages, is . But you could still just look around next time you're stuck in a pediatrician's waiting room. The odds are decent that a copy of Highlights is sitting on the table nearby. Did you ever read Highlights for Children? And did you identify with Goofus, or with Gallant? name: Democrats.org
subject: Happy birthday, Mr. President 🎂
body:
---
Derek, Our president is turning **80 years old today** , and despite his reign of terror, we’re feeling celebratory. Why? name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Minnesota
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Friends,
Today marks one year since Minnesota Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark Hortman, were killed in a targeted and politically motivated shooting — an assassination.
Melissa was a true public servant who dedicated her life to building a better, safer Minnesota. She was a partner and friend to GIFFORDS, and to me. I was on the ground during the legislative session when Minnesota moved several gun safety measures through in 2023, and those measures passed because of her leadership.
My family and I know the horror of a targeted shooting all too well. This cannot be the new normal. Any and all forms of political violence are attacks on democracy itself.
These politically motivated attacks are meant to intimidate us. I am heartbroken, but we will never give up on our work.
One of the most important ways we honor the ones we have lost is by ensuring tragedies like this never happen again, especially on anniversaries like this one.
That is my mission, and the mission of GIFFORDS.
Thank you.
Gabby Giffords
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q22026.A9rDp6&refcode=em260614-1-b&t=1&akid=11552%2E3935704%2EWK3q84)

* * *

**Please take a second to read this...**
As a victim of political violence, Gabby Giffords has led the fight to save lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but she can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to contribute to GIFFORDS PAC today.**

subject: Tough news
body:
I just got out of a meeting with my finance team.
|

| | | |
---
Peter,

I just got out of a meeting with my finance team and have some tough news to share.
Grassroots donations to our campaign have slowed down significantly over the past several days, putting us behind our original projections for this point in the month.
**[If we’re able to raise another $750,000 before our mid-month deadline, we can get back on track. I know this team can get there, so I have to ask: Can I count on your donation to help us close the gap?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk657_v2&amount=10&t=16&akid=1746%2E124072%2EGkOgi6)**

---
My team and I talked through a couple of strategies to get us over this hump.
**We either need to see lots of contributions come through the door today and tomorrow – or we need those who _do_ chip in to give a bit more than usual.**
Normally, we ask folks making their first donation to give just $5. Today, I’m hoping you’ll give a little bit more.
**[With the GOP pouring nearly $100 million so far into this race to defeat me, we can’t afford to keep falling behind on our fundraising – and risk our chances of flipping this seat and the U.S. Senate. Will you chip in $10, or even $15, today?](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk657_v2&amount=10&t=18&akid=1746%2E124072%2EGkOgi6)**

Thanks so much,

Roy

clean_body: Today, President Trump turns 80. Here's what I want to say — and a small way you can be part of it. | Fellow American, Today, June 14th, President Donald Trump turns 80 years old. I'm not going to make this a big fundraising pitch. I just want to take a moment to say something I mean. When President Trump first endorsed me, I made him a promise: I would show up every day and fight for the things that actually matter to the people of Ohio's 15th District. I've kept that promise. And he's kept his to America. | At 80 years old, this man is still in the arena. Still fighting the bureaucrats, the media, and the radical Left — all at once. He didn't have to come back. Fellow American, if you want to show your appreciation for President Trump this birthday, I'd ask for just one small thing today. Chip in just Whatever you can give, I'm grateful. And I know he is too. Happy Birthday, Mr. President. Mike Carey Congressman, OH-15 P.S. Freedom isn't free — and it isn't automatic. It takes people willing to fight for it every single day. 🌈 **_Happy Pride Month_ : The DLCC stands united with the LGBTQ+ community **
As the official arm of the Democratic Party with the sole mission of building Democratic power in state legislatures, the DLCC is on the frontlines of protecting LGBTQ+ rights and freedoms in the states. We are proud to do our part to defend and amplify the voices of the LGBTQ+ community while making sure the GOP’s hateful attacks don’t slip under the radar.
🎉 **_Let's celebrate_ : Representation matters **
❤️ There are **more than 240** openly LGBTQ+ state legislators currently serving in legislatures across the country
🧡 **47 states** now have at least one openly LGBTQ+ state legislator
💛 In **at least 12 states,** LGBTQ+ Democrats are serving as members of chamber leadership
**_🚨 Stay informed:_ Republicans are on the attack **
❌ **Over 500 anti-LGBTQ+ bills** have been introduced just this year – attacking this community has continued to be a mainstay priority for the GOP
❌ **27 GOP-led states have no anti-discrimination state law protections** for gender identity and sexual orientation when it comes to housing, employment, and public accommodations.
❌ **27 states have laws that ban transgender students from participating in sports** consistent with their gender identity. Every single one of those states has a GOP legislative majority.
**👏 Across the country, Democrats are fighting back:**
🌟** _Oregon:_ Democrats enacted legislation to protect professionals who provide gender-affirming care.** Oregon Democrats introduced legislation to protect professionals who provide abortion and gender affirming care. We are proud to do our part to defend and amplify the voices of the LGBTQ+ community while making sure the GOP’s hateful attacks don’t slip under the radar. 🎉 Let's celebrate : Representation matters ❤️ There are more than 240 openly LGBTQ+ state legislators currently serving in legislatures across the country 🧡 47 states now have at least one openly LGBTQ+ state legislator 💛 In at least 12 states, LGBTQ+ Democrats are serving as members of chamber leadership 🚨 Stay informed: Republicans are on the attack ❌ Over 500 anti-LGBTQ+ bills have been introduced just this year – attacking this community has continued to be a mainstay priority for the GOP ❌ 27 GOP-led states have no anti-discrimination state law protections for gender identity and sexual orientation when it comes to housing, employment, and public accommodations. ❌ 27 states have laws that ban transgender students from participating in sports consistent with their gender identity. Dear Friend,

This summer, something is happening that missionaries spend entire careers praying for:

**People from places closed to the gospel will be reachable.**

Fans from Iran, Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Afghanistan, and so many more nations will be accessible to IMB teams. Nations where the gospel is restricted, monitored, or outright illegal will board planes and travel to cities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico to watch soccer.

For a few extraordinary weeks, they will be in places where the gospel can be freely shared.

These are real people, from countries where it’s illegal to talk about Jesus, standing in Fan Zones and stadiums where our teams can freely hand them a Bible, start a conversation, and introduce them to Jesus — often for the first and only time in their lives.

[You can help us reach fans attending the World Cup by giving a gift today.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckbuO2zAURL-G6iTwZUpbqAjsGAgQJwi22O0IirySbyI-QFIr7N8HMuIfSDsHZ4qZt5u-GVwxLD-MhxFL0bloTmkwFWMoJsMOGYz71Jxy1VLVMqlTjiWBrZo3bjxxNsxDAyPrByal7NmpuY9MzbO1kk4c5gHYYOg0n5QApswACqDB8Sikikkm5InJzklhLQM1MDZR2xsi6ZacqdBhKOig2BhTiitWtKWLeWnW8V5rKkR8IfxK-HXf9w79dDDCrwsEyLFg_TxQzKtr7ZZartp6N-FPORxxLbB4CPUcHRBxeTtzRbhKOf4G-wh_fkDO-IDfb-eX93dKOWcvhKutem2NTwaXQMRlt_rhHnGJW7aH8hwKw_IPeXC4eSIu4A2uz5oYKoRKxOXrjelfffvt9bV9ztPk0aUd1xWL6omkyyF2Nvqm_sdfHyP_GwAA___NwqNI)

Here is what your gift does:

Guided by my faith and surrounded by my wife, a high school sweetheart, and our beautiful children, I've experienced firsthand the blessings of America's greatest values.
[My life's mission has been to preserve this American greatness, first by serving in the Air Force and now as a constitutional lawyer fighting anyone who infringes upon our freedom.](https://trk.emails.stayinformednow.)
Yet, I've seen time and time again how fragile our liberty is and the countless evil minds that seek to either take advantage of America or outright destroy it.

[President Trump has seen my commitment to America First, and I am honored to have his 100% endorsement. But the Radical Left is doubling down on its attacks against me because they know America First is their greatest enemy.](https://trk.emails.stayinformednow.)

History may not repeat itself, but it often does rhyme. As resources become valuable, major powers scramble to secure access to them. But it's not just the resources that matter, it's the ability to get (to) them; inevitably, chokepoints emerge, and great powers start jockeying for position. In many cases, success in securing materials or trade routes is enough to reorient global power dynamics.
Rome conquered the Mediterranean in the 2nd century BC because it meant control of trade. For a thousand years (or so), the Silk Road drove empires from the Han Dynasty to the Mongols to battle for control of Central Asian corridors. The spice trade led the Portuguese and the Dutch into conflict over nutmeg in the 1500s and 1600s. The 1908 discovery of oil in Persia redrew the map of the Middle East, and we're still fighting over those lines today. And Britain and Russia spent the entire 19th century playing what [Kipling called the "Great Game" across Central Asia, with India as the grand prize](https://substack.com/redirect/3ac10581-e225-416b-9417-a1c27304b50d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Battles over resources and trading routes is nothing new.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..P-2hbXMXXg1AxvtvA138Sl1Q7N70aqg4ID8xavLOEPk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=201858503)
Today, another Great Game is underway in the north. As I have written before, I believe the next couple of decades will see a Great Power contest for the Arctic, and it is already heating up.
* * *
## [A Coherent Strategy Incoherently Described](https://substack.com/redirect/58abed86-cbca-4a68-9047-63f685b41bf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Many are confused, noting the seeming inconsistency of an America First rhetoric and the use of military force against an adversary. The](https://substack.com/redirect/58abed86-cbca-4a68-9047-63f685b41bf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
Why the Arctic? Well, for starters, it's teeming with valuable resources. The [U.S. Geological Survey estimates](https://substack.com/redirect/7d5e0100-9be4-44bd-bdc5-58f341a6cd4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Arctic holds **90 billion barrels of undiscovered oil** (around 13% of the world's reserves) and **1,670 trillion cubic feet of natural gas** , roughly 30% of the planet's supply. The _[Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/414d0ffe-8af1-4742-a8ab-613e885d5e64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ has estimated](https://substack.com/redirect/414d0ffe-8af1-4742-a8ab-613e885d5e64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) another $1 trillion in rare earth minerals, at today's prices. The Russian Arctic alone holds [$1.5 to $2 trillion in mineral wealth](https://substack.com/redirect/94ab2290-6a62-4bfd-957b-e0ae6d1c5e8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And let's not forget the Arctic already produces 40% of the world's palladium, 20% of its diamonds, and 15% of its platinum.
But it's not just about resources; it's also about transit routes. Readers will know that I've been arguing for months that Trump's seemingly incoherent geopolitical grandstanding about Greenland, the Panama Canal, and Canada aren't random. I've suggested they represent a coherent strategy, albeit incoherently described. But they're also about **chokepoints**.
The global economy runs through a handful of narrow passages: the Strait of Hormuz (oil), the Bab el-Mandeb and Suez Canal (Europe-Asia trade), the Strait of Malacca (China's lifeline), the Panama Canal (Atlantic-Pacific), and the Turkish Straits (Black Sea access). Every major trade route on the planet runs through a bottleneck that a country or alliance can effectively shut.
* * *
## [A Coherent US National Security Strategy](https://substack.com/redirect/27eb3dd1-dbb3-45cb-8d99-74dce62a8479?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

---|---|---
| December 8, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/27eb3dd1-dbb3-45cb-8d99-74dce62a8479?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Regular readers of my work know that I have been closely watching America's foreign policy during Trump's second term. While others saw incoherence or contradictions - destroying drug boats in the Caribbean but not those of the Houthi's in the Red Sea, pulling back from much of the world while getting more engaged in South America, moving on from the Wa...](https://substack.com/redirect/27eb3dd1-dbb3-45cb-8d99-74dce62a8479?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
The Arctic bypasses all of them. The [Northern Sea Route](https://substack.com/redirect/a8304965-293c-4073-89b2-56c29657f45b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), running along Russia's northern coast, shortens the transit time between Asia and Europe by **40%** and saves 4,500 nautical miles--all while avoiding the Suez Canal, the Strait of Hormuz, and the Strait of Malacca. Further, the Northwest Passage through Canadian waters is increasingly safe for transit for more of the year. And Greenland? As you'll see below, It sits at the mouth of both routes. _**Now ask yourself why Trump wants it.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d7bada0e-05ce-4d95-8af7-01a34e9d5f79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

South Korea is so convinced of this future that it [relocated its entire Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries to Busan](https://substack.com/redirect/6607f2ea-2b0a-480c-a8bd-9a5d63f3beea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Seoul, a symbolic but important gesture. The first Korean container ships on the Arctic route are planned for this year. These aren't hypothetical sea lanes that might one day carry goods. They're under construction and the voyages are underway.
As they say, the game is afoot and the main players are ready to go.
**Russia** is already in the Arctic and very active. It has been reopening Soviet-era military bases, building new airfields and ports, and today operates the world's largest icebreaker fleet, including dozens of [nuclear-powered icebreakers](https://substack.com/redirect/4c53fe7a-80d0-4ae6-a15f-1ffe29ee3898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that no other country can match. Russia today controls the Northern Sea Route and [charges transit fees via mandatory icebreaker escorts, permits, and pilotage](https://substack.com/redirect/aa257ab9-2477-4891-bbf8-c5205d2ab88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The Arctic isn't a sideshow for Moscow. It's a part of its strategy.
**China** declared itself a ["near-Arctic state" in 2018](https://substack.com/redirect/aabefeeb-b002-442e-a843-9ada6934b28a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (last I checked it's not near the Arctic, but what do I know?) and outlined a "Polar Silk Road" for Arctic shipping. It has invested heavily in Russia's Northern Sea Route and [started working with Russia to patrol the Bering Strain in 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/aabefeeb-b002-442e-a843-9ada6934b28a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It's even building its own icebreaker fleet. Beijing sees the Arctic the way it sees the South China Sea: contested space where early positioning creates future leverage.
**Canada** has been increasingly focusing on the north and Prime Minister Mark Carney recently announced the government would be investing more than $40 billion in forward operating locations, infrastructure to connect the North, and the development of critical materials. All part of Canada's plan to shift from reliance to resilience, Carney's administration hopes to develop the full economic potential of the region while improving its security footprint. For Canada, the Arctic isn't some faraway and distant worry. It's literally their doorstep.
* * *
## [Time To Defend Greenland](https://substack.com/redirect/07ae920f-1b0c-44c9-8762-1f74ce486923?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[I recently wrote about Canada's military preparing for a possible war with the United States. I suggested we might make sense of the seemingly shocking headline as an effort for global elites in Canada to bolster support for their diversification agenda.](https://substack.com/redirect/07ae920f-1b0c-44c9-8762-1f74ce486923?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
**The United States** is playing catch-up, but Trump's Greenland gambit jumpstarted the conversation about Arctic strategy, and the Pentagon recently deployed F-22s to Alaska. But the clearest measure of the gap: [the U.S. has two operational icebreakers. Russia has over 40](https://substack.com/redirect/4c53fe7a-80d0-4ae6-a15f-1ffe29ee3898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Even Canada, our partner to the north, only has two large icebreakers and six medium sized ones. If freedom of movement through the Arctic is to be maintained, an icebreaker fleet is required.
**NATO** launched [Arctic Sentry](https://substack.com/redirect/aee24eec-a215-43c9-a147-1a466b801008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2026 and gained two Arctic members when Sweden and Finland joined. But Europe's response remains symbolic. As I wrote [earlier this year](https://substack.com/redirect/07ae920f-1b0c-44c9-8762-1f74ce486923?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): The real threat to the Arctic isn't America, it's China and Russia. Europe seems to be posturing against the wrong adversary.
* * *

So, why now? The Arctic and it resources have been there all along, after all. True, but most of it has been inaccessible. **Until now.**
The Arctic is opening in part because the ice is melting. A warmer climate has exposed the oil, the minerals, and the shipping lanes. But it's also a frontier that hasn't been fully exploited, and as the world bifurcates into two global economic and geopolitical blocks, a mad scramble is underway to secure much-needed resources.

#
Hi Peter, it's Tim.
**Donald Trump and his cronies have not stopped attacking me and the progress we’ve made, and I need your help to stand up to them.**
Before I explain more, **[can you chip in $5 to help us reach our $25,000 mid-month fundraising goal?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260614-1.5wCYfO&amount=5&refcode=em20260614-761&t=2&akid=761%2E34582%2EACQU5S)**
Over the past few months, the far-right has continued to come after me — _relentlessly._
Maybe it’s because they just don’t like me, but I think we both know the real reason: they’re afraid of what our people-powered progress means for their dangerous, divisive movement.
Here in Minnesota, we showed everyone what happens when you stand up to Donald Trump and put people first.
We funded free school meals and healthcare, but the robber barons in this administration and their corporate and billionaire donors hate that kind of progress.
_That’s why our movement is under attack._
**I’ll never stop fighting for working families, which is why I’m focused on supporting candidates across the country who are ready to stand with us.** But with the far-right attacks piling up, I can't do it alone.
**[If you’re able, please donate $5 to reject the MAGA agenda and keep us in this fight.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260614-1.5wCYfO&amount=5&refcode=em20260614-761&t=3&akid=761%2E34582%2EACQU5S)**

Tim Walz

Republicans are escalating their attacks on democracy to lock control of Congress in their hands for the foreseeable future. **That’s why the first pillar of our plan is to fight back anywhere and everywhere Republicans try to manipulate maps in their favor. But we also understand that’s only part of the fight. The NDRC is working to counter Republican gerrymandering in states like California, Colorado, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Utah, and Virginia.** Here’s how we plan to get it done:

Use advanced demographic data analysis to implement more durable maps that 1) protect communities and democracy, and 2) produce a fortified foundation against future efforts to lock in an insurmountable Republican advantage. Work with voters to pass new maps and reforms that ensure states can respond faster and more aggressively to Trump’s mid-decade gerrymanders. Make no mistake — this is grueling work that requires a massive amount of resources. body:

Peter,

Before we ask you to [ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260614-movement.uVfqCR&refcode=em20260614-2361&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=2361%2E342411%2EIsQVgM ]chip in $3 ahead of tomorrow’s
mid-month fundraising deadline, we want to be straight with you about
what's at stake.

MAGA extremists and their billionaire backers will do anything in their
power to unseat the Squad. Dark money groups are flooding the arena with
cash trying to drown out our movement, and they're not slowing down.

Why? Because Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida refuse to be bought,
bullied, or silenced.

The Squad doesn’t take corporate PAC money. They don't water down their
convictions when the pressure gets intense. They show up for working
people, immigrant communities, and everyone the establishment would rather
ignore — speaking truth to power and fighting for justice on all fronts.

That’s exactly why the Squad is under attack.

The Squad Victory Fund was built to defend our progressive champions and
keep this movement strong. We’re not funded by billionaires or backed by
corporate interests. We’re built by people like you who believe this
movement is worth fighting for.

Our mid-month fundraising deadline is tomorrow night, and we can't afford
to fall short. If we don't hit our goal, we go into the next phase of this
fight with fewer resources to push back on attacks, less capacity to
organize, and a harder road to protecting these seats.

Slowing down at a time where we need to be our strongest is not an option.
That’s where you come in,
Peter.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260614-movement.uVfqCR&refcode=em20260614-2361&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1003&akid=2361%2E342411%2EIsQVgM ]Will you chip in $3 to the Squad Victory Fund today
ahead of tomorrow’s mid-month deadline and ensure our progressive
champions have what they need to stay in the fight?

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20260614-movement.uVfqCR&refcode=em20260614-2361&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1022&akid=2361%2E342411%2EIsQVgM ]Contribute ››

In solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.squadvictoryfund.com/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=2361%2E342411%2EIsQVgM

In addition to what’s legally required, The Squad Victory Fund does not accept contributions from: (1) corporations, associations, or their PACs; (2) individuals registered as federal lobbyists or under FARA; (3) from the PACs, lobbyists, or SEC-named executives of fossil fuel companies; or (4) from the Fraternal Order of Police.

Contributions or gifts to The Squad Victory Fund are not tax deductible.

Contributions to The Squad Victory Fund will be allocated equally among: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, Rashida Tlaib for Congress, Courage to Change, Inspiring Leadership Has a Name PAC, Power of Us PAC, and Rooted in Community Leadership PAC.

Any contributor may designate their contribution for a particular participant. The allocation formula above may change if any contributor makes a contribution that, when allocated, would exceed the amount that the contributor may lawfully give to any participant.

After contributing to The Squad Victory Fund, you will automatically be signed up to receive email updates from Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress, Ilhan for Congress, The Committee to Elect Ayanna Pressley, and Rashida Tlaib for Congress. You may of course opt-out by unsubscribing at any time.

To contribute via check, please address to The Squad Victory Fund c/o MBA Consulting Group, PO Box 15845, Washington D.C., 20003

_**The good news:**_ A federal judge knocked President Trump's executive order ending federal funding for NPR and PBS, saying it violated the broadcasters' First Amendment rights.

_**The bad news:**_ Trump cut $1.1 billion for public media outlets that he and Congress had earlier agreed to, **and this ruling doesn’t automatically guarantee that broadcasters will receive the funding they need to function.**

Hey, it’s Rob Sand with some great news:

**I’m officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of Iowa.**

I’ve been traveling to all 99 counties every year since I ran for Auditor back in 2017. There’s one thing EVERYBODY — Democrat, Republican, independent, etc. — can agree on: **the status quo is failing the majority of Iowans.**

We’re in the grips of a generational farm crisis, mass layoffs, education cuts, rising cancer rates, rural hospital closures, brain drain, and **an economy that is now the worst in the country.**

Iowans are fighting an uphill battle just to make ends meet. They’re tired, and tired of fighting.

This race is a toss-up, according to the experts at _Cook Political Report_ , **because we’ve built one of the broadest bipartisan coalitions in American politics**. That’s why the choice we face in this election is so much more than (D) or (R). It’s between a divisive culture warrior or a proven public servant who brings people together.

I believe Iowans will see the contrast, but winning requires us to be realistic about the challenges we’re facing. **Our success depends on whether we can sustain our incredible grassroots energy in the months ahead.**

The decisions of over 60,000 small-dollar donors to invest in this campaign propelled us to this moment. Now I’m asking each and every one of you to become one of the first founding donors of my general election campaign.

[_**Will you split a donation between my campaign and Abigail Spanberger's United for Virginia's Future PAC to help win this toss-up governor's race and put Iowa on the path to recovery?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133316512/627454362/733988564?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-06-14_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWQ3N2QxYzQtMDE2OC1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2ZsaheypDTZLQNBSPc44Nb3qsg1h24rj2qmWkNV34BA=)

Together, we’re going to make history.

So much gratitude,
Rob Sand

I want to be real with you for a minute:
What we're up against is no joke.
On the other side of this race sits an entrenched MAGA candidate with a Rolodex full of millionaire and billionaire backers, a network of dark money groups, and the full weight of the Republican establishment behind them.
They've done this before. They know how to leverage fear and political games to win. And they are not taking us lightly.
They watched us sweep every parish in round one, and they picked up the phone. They started making calls. Cutting checks. Building the kind of war chest that's supposed to make campaigns like ours fold up and go home.
That's how they keep power. They make the cost of challenging them so high that most people don't even try.
I'm not most people. I'm a farmer who's spent a lifetime doing hard things, and we’re starting to generate national attention on this race. But attention alone won’t get the job done.
We need resources to get our message to every corner of this state. To make sure voters know the runoff is happening and what's at stake. To counter the inevitable wave of MAGA attack ads that are already being planned.
I've talked to Republicans who are quietly rooting for us. Independents who've never voted Democrat who are reconsidering. Lifelong Louisianans who are done watching their state bleed jobs, farms, and dignity while career politicians in Washington serve their donors instead of their constituents.
That coalition can win. I've seen it with my own eyes on this campaign trail.
But it only comes together if we have the resources to reach those voters. And that's where you come in.
Every dollar you give right now is a direct counterweight to MAGA's millionaire backers. It's proof that this movement is real. That we're serious. That we're not going anywhere.

Democrat consulting firm BerlinRosen has built an impressive list of radical left clients sympathetic to Islamist causes, many of whom are also obsessed with "Getting Trump."
Many of BerlinRosen's congressional clients supported the left's impeachment scam against President Trump or supported groups that did. More recently, some of these same clients have called for the 25th Amendment to be weaponized against President Trump. Clients like Color of Change cheered on Alvin Bragg's politically motivated prosecution of President Trump. Others supported Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign. This is in addition to the antisemitic groups the firm has worked with BerlinRosen.

---|---|---
So why does Kushner Companies still work with BerlinRosen via M18 PR, which Kushner Companies has retained for several of their real estate projects? M18 PR, a leading boutique public relations agency specializing in real estate, hospitality, and design, was [acquired ](https://substack.com/redirect/5aef93fd-d86f-469c-b460-af2ca5764a5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)by BerlinRosen in 2023. Both firms now operate under BerlinRosen's parent holding company, Orchestra.
Jared Kushner is President Trump's son-in-law. He is also tasked with negotiating peace deals and trade deals across the globe as part of President Trump's America First agenda.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/17267d3a-b036-4fb3-9b24-12d17356008c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Several BerlinRosen congressional clients have ramped up efforts to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove President Trump from office. In April 2026, Rep. Dan Goldman publicly [stated](https://substack.com/redirect/62a4cd07-ad47-49c9-895e-7e3b4ebc47b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> _" Trump is not well. We need the 25th amendment before something really bad happens on US soil."_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3cbc2f78-77af-4f25-80de-caa2db409237?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

---|---|---
The 25th Amendment should only be used under dire circumstances to remove a president who is truly incapacitated. The closest call was over 100 years ago, when Woodrow Wilson was incapacitated by a stroke and his wife, Edith Wilson, quietly took over some of his duties.
The 25th Amendment should not be used for partisan political purposes. But that has not stopped congressional Democrats from twisting the Constitution to advance their own political goals.
Rep. Summer Lee took to X,[ posting](https://substack.com/redirect/9294b9d4-5a7a-41fe-81b7-9c0d604de9f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> _" This is sick and twisted from anyone, much less the president of the United States. Trump's genocidal language and indiscriminate warfare cannot be normalized or accepted. He should be removed from office."_
It is quite ironic how Rep. Lee refers to President Trump as 'sick and twisted' while Lee herself can't disavow the pro-open border riots at Delaney Hall in New Jersey. And every voter we register starts with the same investment – $26. 20+ years of organizing have proved that it costs just $26 to register one voter. That’s a small price to pay for the chance to flip who holds power in Washington. So with this in mind, Peter: Thank you, Voto Latino

We have a historic responsibility to organize against this corrupt presidency
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2274%2E791427%2EbxAM7H)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260614-1-180&t=2&akid=2274%2E791427%2EbxAM7H)
Friend — I told _The Washington Post_ exactly what I told you.
**I will never back down to Trump, despite his constant attacks and sham investigations.**
Because, as racist and unbecoming as his attacks on me are, they pale in comparison to the damage being done by his administration and his party’s far-right policies.
Under Trump’s reign of terror, I have seen my community targeted, demonized, harassed, pepper-sprayed, zip-tied, beaten, arrested, and detained without charges.
Trump is going after his political enemies and entire groups of people that his hateful Republican allies want to silence, and he’s using ICE as his personal police force and the DOJ as his personal prosecutors to carry out those goals.
**We have a historic responsibility to organize against this corrupt presidency and protect our communities from harm.**
In countries across the world, fascism and totalitarianism have been defeated through the sheer determination of democracy and mass movements.
That’s why I’m laser-focused on building progressive power, from our neighborhoods here in Minneapolis to the halls of Congress, pushing towards November’s midterm elections as our chance to strike a fatal blow to Trump’s ability to carry out his agenda.
The best way you can help us propel this movement forward in the face of Trump’s constant attacks is to chip in and financially support our efforts to win big next year.
[**Please, friend: Make a contribution of $10 or whatever you can afford today and stand by my side as we fight back. We all have a role to play in defeating hate and authoritarianism. I’m hoping I can count on you to do your part, whatever that may be.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jun26.ltbpUI&refcode=em260614-1-180&t=3&akid=2274%2E791427%2EbxAM7H)

[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Justice Democrat Melat Kiros has her 15-term incumbent opponent, Rep.
Diana DeGette, and her corporate backers panicking.

A brand new super PAC just appeared out of nowhere and dropped $350,000 on
digital ads against Melat in Colorado’s 1st district.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260614-mk.u6Afjx&refcode=em20260614-37907&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=37907%2E1203867%2E1h66vu ]Tweet by Melat Kiros for Congress, CO-01: They formed a super PAC
overnight to spend $350K against us. Whether it’s AIPAC, AI, or big
Pharma, they’re used to buying and owning this seat, and now they’re
hiding from the voters to do it. Denver is about to remind them that this
seat belongs to us.

For decades, Do-nothing Democrats like DeGette have relied on corporate
cash to stay in power while working families are left behind waiting for
the change this moment demands. And when they’re threatened by a
grassroots movement like ours, they spend more to drown us out.

DeGette has remained in power all these years thanks to campaign checks
and outside spending from Big Pharma and the real estate lobby — and she
doesn’t have much to show for it.

Melat represents the change people want — leadership willing to challenge
the status quo instead of protecting it.

Like every Justice Democrat, she rejects corporate PAC money because she
believes elected officials should answer to the people they represent, not
corporations buying their seats.

Friend, Did you get a chance to read yesterday’s email? I wanted to update you on what I’ve been up to in Congress lately. We’re building essential momentum to end U.S. support for the genocidal war on Lebanon, with over 90 members of Congress voting for my War Powers Resolution last week.
